origin.place: Khorasan (eastern Persia / modern Afghanistan-Iran border region)

_quarry.description: The Persian geographer al-Istakhri documented vertical-axis windmills in Khorasan by the 10th century; the panemone design used six to twelve cloth or reed sails rotating around a vertical shaft to grind grain. The first documented European windmill was recorded at Weedley, Yorkshire, in 1185, followed rapidly by mills in Normandy and Flanders. European horizontal-axis post mills differ structurally from Persian designs, and scholars debate whether this represents independent invention or knowledge transmitted via returning Crusaders.
